items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Others that I heard in Cincy that had big names where "Speed" Webb and Alfonso Trent and Bellson, an orchestra from West Virginia and [that] Bobby Robinson and John Nesbit had played with.

ctx.x: Some months after, "Jelly Roll" came back to Cincinnati with the orchestra of Fate Marable. Fate played piano also but he directed the band most of the time. I never knew who the musicians were in this orchestra, but me and everyone that heard them knew that we had heard one of the best jazz orchestras that had come to town in those days, and I always found a way to hear the bands that came along.
Others that I heard in Cincy that had big names where "Speed" Webb and Alfonso Trent and Bellson, an orchestra from West Virginia and [that] Bobby Robinson and John Nesbit had played with.

Helvey took a job across the river in Newport, Ky., at a Road House and a new drummer joined the orchestra. Towles left with a T.O.B.A. show called the Whitman? Westman Sisters. I had seen this show in Cincinnati and I remember that one of the sisters named Alice was a wonderful tap dancer. The new drummer was John Hargrave and he was a better drummer than Towles.
